input.area: Unicode / CJK / mixed-script behavior + stress & adversarial inputs (Python-Markdown 3.10.2, no extensions)

rules.rule: Output is raw UTF-8. Non-ASCII characters (CJK, full-width punctuation, emoji, RTL, combining marks) are NEVER escaped, entity-encoded, percent-encoded, or Unicode-normalized. They pass through byte-identically in paragraph text, headers, list items, blockquotes, code spans, code blocks, link text, link hrefs and titles, and HTML attributes. Only `&`, `<`, `>` are escaped (and `"` inside attribute values). Implementation note: do NOT call String.prototype.normalize() anywhere.

WORD-CHARACTER CLASS (`\w`) — the single most important Unicode decision. Python's `\w` is used for the smart-underscore-emphasis lookarounds. Define isWord(cp) = (Unicode general category of cp is one of Lu, Ll, Lt, Lm, Lo, Nd, Nl, No) OR cp === 0x5F ('_'). Equivalently: `Py_UNICODE_ISALNUM(cp) || cp === '_'`, i.e. Python's `str.isalnum()`. Consequences: ALL CJK ideographs, Hiragana/Katakana, Hangul, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, full-width Latin letters AND full-width digits, U+3005 々 (Lm), U+3006 〆 (Lo), U+3007 〇 (Nl), U+30FC ー (Lm), U+00B9 ¹ (No), U+2177 ⅷ (Nl) ARE word characters. NOT word characters: emoji and all So/Sm/Sc/Sk symbols (😀 🀄 ☃ ± § ¥ = +), all combining marks Mn/Mc (U+0301, U+3099, U+0E31, U+FE0F VS16), all format chars Cf (U+200E LRM, U+200F RLM, U+200B ZWSP, U+FEFF, U+200D ZWJ), all Zs/whitespace, U+30FB ・ (Po). CRITICAL for JS: this must be evaluated per CODE POINT, not per UTF-16 unit — astral-plane letters (U+1D400 𝐀 Lu, U+2000B 𠀋 Lo, U+104B0 𐒰 Lu, U+1D7D9 𝟙 Nd) ARE word chars, while astral symbols (U+1F004 🀄 So) are not. JS `\w` is ASCII-only and is NOT a substitute; a `[\p{L}\p{Nd}\p{Nl}\p{No}_]` /u class is the correct equivalent.

SMART UNDERSCORE EMPHASIS pattern is exactly `(?<!\w)(_)(?!_)(.+?)(?<!_)\1(?!\w)` (and strong: `(?<!\w)(__)(?!_)(.+?)(?<!_)\1(?!\w)`), with `\w` per the rule above and LAZY `.+?` that BACKTRACKS/expands until the trailing `(?!\w)` is satisfied. So `_中_文_字_` matches with content `中_文_字` (the parser tries `中`, fails `(?!\w)` on 文; tries `中_文`, fails on 字; then `中_文_字` succeeds at end-of-string). `中文_下_线` fails on BOTH lookarounds (leading 文 is \w, trailing 线 is \w) → literal. `中文_下_ 线` still fails only on the leading lookbehind → literal, proving CJK is \w for the lookbehind. `😀_a_ b` succeeds (😀 not \w, space not \w). `😀_a_b` fails only on the trailing `(?!\w)` (b is \w) and no expansion is possible → literal.

ASTERISK emphasis/strong have NO word-boundary rule at all (patterns are `(\*)([^\*]+)\1` for em and `(\*{2})(.+?)\1` for strong). CJK directly adjacent to `*` on either side always works. So `中*文*字` → em, while `中_文_字` → literal. `*中*文*字*` yields `中文字` because the em pattern's content class `[^\*]+` cannot cross an asterisk (contrast with the underscore pattern's `.+?` which can).

WHITESPACE CLASS (`\s` in regexes and the strip family). Python's whitespace set is: U+0009-U+000D, U+001C, U+001D, U+001E, U+001F, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000. NOT whitespace: U+FEFF and U+200B. This differs from JS in two directions: JS `\s`/`trim()` include U+FEFF (must be excluded) and exclude U+0085 and U+001C-U+001F (must be included). Verified via the NOT_STRONG_RE rule `((^|\s)(\*{1,3}|_{1,3})(?=\s|$))`, which converts a lone asterisk/underscore run surrounded by whitespace into literal text: for every char in the set, `A<c>*<c>B<c>*<c>C` leaves the asterisks literal; for U+FEFF and U+200B it produces `<em>`.

BLANK-LINE / block-splitting is ASCII-only, but block EMPTINESS uses Unicode whitespace. (a) The normalize-whitespace preprocessor's `re.sub(r'(?<=
) +
', '
', src)` matches ASCII U+0020 ONLY: a line containing any Unicode space (U+00A0, U+3000, U+2003, U+1680, U+202F, U+205F, U+2028, U+2029, U+0085, U+000B, U+000C, U+001C, U+001F) does NOT become a blank line and does not split a paragraph; the character is preserved verbatim in the paragraph text. (b) But a block whose content is empty after Python-Unicode `.strip()` is dropped entirely, so a document consisting solely of such a character produces EMPTY output. U+FEFF and U+200B are not whitespace and therefore survive as a one-character paragraph.

STRIP SIDEDNESS per block type, all using the Python Unicode whitespace set. (a) Paragraph: `p.text = block.lstrip()` — leading Unicode whitespace REMOVED, trailing PRESERVED. (b) ATX header: `.strip()` — removed on BOTH sides. (c) List item text and blockquote paragraph text: lstrip only — trailing Unicode whitespace PRESERVED. (d) Indented code block: `.rstrip()` then a single `\n` appended — trailing Unicode whitespace REMOVED, LEADING preserved. U+FEFF/U+200B are never stripped anywhere.

DIGIT CLASS (`\d`) for the ordered-list marker `^[ ]{0,3}\d+\.[ ]+` is Unicode category Nd ONLY (decimal digits), evaluated per code point (astral Nd counts). Full-width digits (U+FF10-FF19), Arabic-Indic (U+0663), Extended Arabic-Indic (U+06F3), Devanagari (U+0969), Tibetan (U+0F22), Limbu (U+1946) and MATHEMATICAL DOUBLE-STRUCK ONE (U+1D7D9) all START AN ORDERED LIST. Nl and No do NOT: U+3007 〇, U+2166 Ⅶ, U+00B2 ² stay literal, as do Lo numerals like 一. Digit scripts may be mixed freely within one `\d+` run and across list items. No `start` attribute is ever emitted regardless of the number. JS `\d` is ASCII-only — use `\p{Nd}` with the /u flag.

All BLOCK MARKER characters are strictly ASCII; full-width look-alikes are inert literal text. ＊ (U+FF0A), ＃ (U+FF03), ＞ (U+FF1E), － (U+FF0D), ｜ (U+FF5C), ｀ (U+FF40), ［］ (U+FF3B/FF3D), （） (U+FF08/FF09) never trigger emphasis, headers, blockquotes, lists, hr, code spans, or links. Likewise the SPACE required after a marker must be ASCII U+0020: `-　中` and `1.　项` are plain paragraphs (regexes `[*+-][ ]+` and `\.[ ]+`). Exceptions where a Unicode space still works: (a) ATX headers need no space at all (`#中文` → h1) and the leading Unicode space ends up inside the header text which is then `.strip()`ed; (b) blockquote is `^[ ]{0,3}>[ ]?(.*)` so `>　中` works — the U+3000 becomes part of the content and is then removed by the paragraph lstrip.

TAB EXPANSION is `expandtabs(4)` counted in CODE POINTS, not display columns. A CJK ideograph occupies exactly ONE column even though it is double-width visually. `中\tx` → 中 at column 0, tab at column 1, next stop 4 → THREE spaces. `中中中中\tx` → tab at column 4, next stop 8 → FOUR spaces. This also means a tab after 1-3 CJK chars can become the trailing 2+ spaces that generate `
`. Astral characters count as ONE column (iterate code points, not UTF-16 units).

LINE-BREAK NORMALIZATION only touches CR: `
` → `
` then `` → `
`. U+0085 NEL, U+000B VT, U+000C FF, U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR are NOT line terminators — they remain inside the paragraph text verbatim and do not split blocks (Python uses `.split('
')`, not `.splitlines()`). Additionally U+0002 (STX) and U+0003 (ETX) are DELETED from the source before parsing (they are the internal placeholder sentinels), so `abc` renders as `abc` and a document of only U+0002 is empty; placeholder injection is therefore impossible.

AUTOMAIL (`<...@...>`, regex `<([^<> !]*@[^@<> ]*)>`) accepts arbitrary non-ASCII including CJK and emoji, and entity-encodes EVERY character. Two DIFFERENT encodings are used: (a) the link TEXT encodes each code point via HTML entity NAME if one exists in Python's `html.entities.codepoint2name`, else `&#<decimal>;` — so `¥`→`¥`, `é`→`é`, `&`→`&`, CJK→`中`; (b) the `href` is `mailto:` + email with EVERY code point unconditionally as `&#<decimal>;` (never a name). Iteration is per CODE POINT: 😀 becomes the single entity `😀` (JS must use codePointAt / for-of, not charCodeAt). A leading literal `mailto:` in the source is stripped before encoding.

AUTOLINK `<scheme://...>` (regex `<((?:[Ff]|[Hh][Tt])[Tt][Pp][Ss]?://[^<>]*)>`) leaves non-ASCII COMPLETELY UNTOUCHED in both href and text — no percent-encoding, no IDNA/punycode. A `<...>` containing non-ASCII that is neither an autolink nor an email is not recognized as an HTML tag and is escaped to `<...>` (the raw-HTML tag-name matcher is ASCII-letter-only).

HTML ENTITY PASSTHROUGH is matched by an ASCII-ONLY pattern equivalent to `&(#[0-9]+|#x[0-9a-fA-F]+|[a-zA-Z0-9]+);`. A match is emitted verbatim (validity of the name is NOT checked — `&unknown;` survives). Any other `&` is escaped to `&`. Consequently `&中;` → `&中;` and a numeric entity written with FULL-WIDTH digits `&#１１１;` is not an entity → `&#１１１;`. CJK can never form an entity name.

REFERENCE-LINK ID FOLDING uses Python `str.lower()`, which is equivalent to JS `String.prototype.toLowerCase()` for every case probed, INCLUDING the Greek final-sigma special-casing (CPython special-cases U+03A3 with the Final_Sigma context rule, exactly like the ECMAScript algorithm): `[ΑΣ][]` matches a definition written `[ας]` (final sigma) and does NOT match `[ασ]`. Also verified equivalent for ẞ→ß, İ→i+U+0307, KELVIN SIGN U+212A→k, full-width Ａ→ａ. CJK is unaffected by lower(). Use `toLowerCase()` (never `toLocaleLowerCase()`). Separately: the DEFINITION's id is `.strip()`ed with Python Unicode whitespace, but the id at the USE site is NOT stripped — `[ 中文 ][]` and even `[ 中文 ][]` fail to resolve against `[中文]:`.

The LINK-DEFINITION separator after `[id]:` is `[ ]*` — ASCII spaces only. `[a]:　http://x` and `[a]: http://x` are NOT definitions and remain literal paragraphs (and the reference then fails to resolve). Conversely, inline link URLs are taken verbatim including any Unicode space: `[a](http://x　y)` yields `href="http://x　y"`.

HARD LINE BREAK: a line ending in TWO OR MORE ASCII spaces followed by another line in the same block emits `
